item.title: U2 Get Drenched, Tap Into Classic, Soaring Sound in Video For Funky ‘Street of Dreams’ Single
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome back to Trending on Billboard! Today, we're excited to share the latest news from iconic rock band U2. The group has just dropped a brand new single, "Street of Dreams", accompanied by a captivating music video that's got everyone talking.
[Clip of "Street of Dreams" plays in the background]
Host: The song is the first taste of their upcoming studio album, their first since 2017's Songs of Experience. And what a return it is! The soaring, triumphal track features Bono's uplifting vocals and The Edge's signature shimmery guitar work.
[Clip of the music video plays]
Host: The video, filmed in Mexico City, shows the band performing on a spray-painted bus, with Bono chanting the song's title in Spanish. The visuals are stunning, with the band jamming out in the streets and on a balcony, despite the threat of storms.
Host: But what's really interesting is the story behind the video shoot. The band was in Mexico City for the 2026 Street Child World Cup Finals Tournament, and they filmed the video on the fly, with a massive crowd gathering to watch. And when a thunderstorm caused a generator to crash, the band took refuge on a local family's balcony to finish the shoot.
[Clip of the band on the balcony plays]
Host: The result is a heartfelt, energetic video that's a love letter to the people of Mexico. The final shot shows the band walking down a lonely road, with the caption "Gracias a la gente de Mexico" - thank you to the people of Mexico.
Host: "Street of Dreams" is just the beginning of what's to come from U2. Their new album, produced by Jackknife Lee, is due out later this year, following their surprise EPs Easter Lily and Days of Ash. We can't wait to hear more from this legendary band.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today's episode of Trending on Billboard. Thanks for tuning in!
